title: Classic Aussie Sausage Rolls
description: The Aussie snack king — perfect for footy days, picnics, or anytime hunger strikes.

ingredients.notes: lean or heart smart is best

youWillNeed.note: Makes portion control and even distribution much easier.

method.instruction: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line baking trays with baking paper.
In a large bowl, combine beef & sausage mince, bread crumbs, diced onion, grated carrot, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix until well combined.
Place the meat mixture in a piping bag, pipe along the edge of each pastry strip and roll tightly, seam side down. Cut off excess pastry.
Cut each roll into approximately 12-14 cm lengths. Place on the prepared trays.
Brush tops with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and puffed. Serve hot with tomato sauce.

notes.title: Beef Mince
notes.content: Get the best mince you can afford... the less fat content the better.

notes.title: Sausage Mince
notes.content: Buy from the butcher, tends to be less fatty than store bought.

notes.title: Excess Pastry
notes.content: Can be used to make child sized Sausage Rolls.

notes.title: Flavour Boost
notes.content: Add grated cheese, a squirt of BBQ sauce, or a spoonful of chutney inside the rolls for an extra flavour kick.

notes.title: Make-Ahead
notes.content: Assemble rolls unbaked and freeze on a tray. Once frozen, transfer to a bag. Bake from frozen, adding 10 minutes to the cooking time.

notes.title: Piping Bag
notes.content: You can get a piping bag kit from woolworths for about $4. It contains 6 thick, strong bags and 4 tips... you do not need the tips for this. Just cut the bottom off.

journal.content: I used the Woolworths brand of Sausage Mince and found it was too fatty for my liking... The flavour is good and is what I expected. Keep an eye out for the next journal entry.
